newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIA LATE RUBBER DOWN, SINGAPORE DEALERS BUY.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIA LATE RUBBER DOWN, SINGAPORE DEALERS BUY.

text.p: Indonesian rubber prices were lower in late trading on Thursday, with Singapore dealers picking up some tyre-grade SIR20, traders said.
They said October shipment SIR20 was done at 43.50 cents fob Medan while November rubber was done at 43.75 cents. There was a bid for September SIR20 at 43.25 cents but no deal was heard.
Singapore dealers also bought September SIR20 at 42.75 cents/lb fob Palembang, and November shipments at 43.25 cents.
"Prices are easing because of the prevailing bearish sentiment following news of the Thai stock levels," one trader said, adding that tyre-makers were absent from the market.
"Tyre-makers are mostly covered for October," he said.

The traders also said a move by members of the Association of Natural Rubber Producing Countries to cut back supplies in a bid to boost prices was unlikely to find support in Indonesia, the world's top producer after Thailand.
Sucharit Promdej, an advisor to the Thai agriculture ministry, said the idea was floated during a three-day meeting of the grouping in Thailand that ended on Thursday.

The Coordinating Committee on Production and Marketing Strategies meeting suggested member countries should lobby the private sector to hold bigger commercial stocks and recommended that governments introduce tapping holidays.

"Controlling tapping will be difficult in Indonesia because it is the livelihood of most smallholders," one trader said. "Interest rates in Indonesia are also very high, and holding large stocks could be costly."
Traders said that October SIR20 was offered at 43.50 cents fob Medan, 43.00-43.25 cents fob Palembang, Padang and Surabaya.
